actions.action: Reserve storage exclusively for critical history
actions.mechanism: Separate capacity prevents ordinary-event pressure from evicting critical records during the bounded outage.
actions.implementation: Reserve 2 MB for critical data plus worst-case encoding and recovery overhead; allocate ordinary storage only from the remaining 20 MB.
actions.check: Inject maximum-rate ordinary traffic and 2 MB of critical events across 30 minutes; verify every critical sequence survives within quota.
actions.risk: Unbudgeted framing, filesystem allocation, or temporary files can invalidate the reservation.

actions.action: Sanitize diagnostics before they enter storage
actions.mechanism: An allowlisted event schema prevents prohibited content from reaching any telemetry persistence path.
actions.implementation: Encode only approved event codes, sequence identifiers, timestamps, and bounded numeric fields. Reject arbitrary strings; apply the same rules to summaries.
actions.check: Inject message bodies, credentials, and user-content canaries into every input field; verify none appear in buffers, journals, or upload payloads.
actions.risk: Exception traces and diagnostic logging can bypass the main encoder.

actions.action: Preserve recent ordinary detail with explicit reduction markers
actions.mechanism: A bounded ordinary-event ring sacrifices older detail while fixed-size coverage metadata identifies affected periods.
actions.implementation: Assign ordinary sequence numbers before admission. Maintain fixed time buckets containing sequence bounds, counts, and reduction flags; persist flags before overwriting records.
actions.check: Overflow the ring repeatedly; verify every omitted ordinary event belongs to a flagged bucket and intact buckets contain their expected sequences.
actions.risk: Bucket markers identify coarse affected intervals, not necessarily individual missing runs.

actions.action: Aggregate repetitive ordinary events under pressure
actions.mechanism: Fixed-size summaries retain event frequency while avoiding storage of every repeated occurrence.
actions.implementation: At a byte watermark, replace ordinary occurrences with per-code, per-minute counts and first/last sequence bounds. Use a bounded code table and overflow counter.
actions.check: Replay a known event distribution; verify summary totals match inputs and coverage metadata labels aggregated intervals as reduced detail.
actions.risk: Aggregation loses ordering and correlation; never apply it to critical events.

actions.action: Make local commits recoverable without doubling storage
actions.mechanism: Checksummed records and ordered commit metadata distinguish complete writes from interrupted writes while preserving committed critical history.
actions.implementation: Use preallocated segments and alternating checksummed headers. Durably commit critical records before reporting acceptance; prohibit critical-segment reuse before acknowledgement.
actions.check: Terminate the process at each write boundary; restart and verify all accepted critical sequences remain readable and allocated storage stays within quota.
actions.risk: Power-loss guarantees depend on actual filesystem and storage flush behavior.

actions.action: Make retries idempotent and acknowledgements explicit
actions.mechanism: Stable record identities separate duplicated deliveries from distinct events and prevent premature local deletion.
actions.implementation: Identify records by installation epoch, stream, and sequence. Deduplicate transactionally at the recipient; reclaim critical records only after durable acknowledgement.
actions.check: Drop acknowledgements, reorder batches, and resend them; verify one logical copy per identity and retention of every unacknowledged critical record.
actions.risk: Deduplication retention must cover the sender’s retry horizon.

actions.action: Upload coverage manifests alongside retained records
actions.mechanism: A bounded manifest declares expected sequence coverage, allowing recipients to distinguish intentional reduction from unexplained gaps.
actions.implementation: Snapshot each upload generation’s stream bounds and reduction buckets. Acknowledge its manifest and records together before recycling associated metadata.
actions.check: Remove one critical record and duplicate another during replay; verify the recipient reports a missing sequence separately from a duplicate identity.
actions.risk: Without a manifest, a missing final record may be invisible.

actions.action: Exercise the complete outage and recovery boundary
actions.mechanism: A deterministic fault-injection replay checks preservation, reduction reporting, privacy, and retry behavior together rather than independently.
actions.implementation: Generate 30 minutes of traffic with ordinary pressure at the stated rate and 2 MB critical volume; reconnect with dropped, repeated, and reordered uploads.
actions.check: Assert complete critical sequence coverage, marked ordinary reductions, duplicate detection, no prohibited canaries, and peak allocated storage at or below 20 MB.
actions.risk: Do not extrapolate results to longer outages or unrestricted critical volume.
